manual.warlockery.conjuration.doll.title: Doll: Use
manual.warlockery.conjuration.doll: Craft a blank Doll from wool and string, then combine it with the ingredient shown on a specialized doll's recipe page. A blank Doll is only a crafting vessel and has no bound effect.
manual.warlockery.conjuration.earth_guar: Use in the air to bind this doll to yourself, or use it on another player to bind them. Keep it in the bound player's inventory or a loaded Doll Shelf. It spends durability to prevent one lethal fall, Elytra collision, dripstone impact, falling-block crush, or mace smash, then grants Slow Falling.
manual.warlockery.conjuration.water_guar: Use in the air to bind this doll to yourself, or use it on another player to bind them. Keep it in the bound player's inventory or a loaded Doll Shelf. It spends durability to prevent one lethal drowning hit, restores air, and grants Water Breathing.
manual.warlockery.conjuration.hunger_gua: Use in the air to bind this doll to yourself, or use it on another player to bind them. Keep it in the bound player's inventory or a loaded Doll Shelf. It spends durability to prevent one lethal starvation hit and restores food and saturation.
manual.warlockery.conjuration.fire_guard: Use in the air to bind this doll to yourself, or use it on another player to bind them. Keep it in the bound player's inventory or a loaded Doll Shelf. It spends durability to prevent one lethal fire or lava hit, grants Fire Resistance, and seeks safe footing after lava.
manual.warlockery.conjuration.tool_mendi: Use in the air to bind this doll to yourself, or use it on another player to bind them. Keep it in that player's inventory or a loaded Doll Shelf. While its bound player is online, it periodically spends one doll durability to repair two durability on a damaged item held in either hand.
manual.warlockery.conjuration.death_guar: Use in the air to bind this doll to yourself, or use it on another player to bind them. Keep it in the bound player's inventory or a loaded Doll Shelf. It spends durability to prevent an otherwise lethal hit and gives the normal Totem recovery effects. A matching elemental guard is chosen before this general guard.
manual.warlockery.conjuration.hex_guard_: Use in the air to bind this doll to yourself, or use it on another player to bind them. Keep it in the bound player's inventory or a loaded Doll Shelf. It spends durability to block hostile hexes aimed at that target and may answer a known attacker with lightning.
manual.warlockery.conjuration.hexing_dol: Use this doll on a living target to bind it. While holding the bound doll, Shift-use in the air to cycle Prick, Shove, Ignite, and Drown; use normally in the air to apply the selected action at range. The target must be alive and available to the server. Wards and Hex Guard Dolls can block the action, but every attempt spends doll durability.
manual.warlockery.conjuration.blood_link: Use this doll on another player to bind them, then keep it in your inventory. While both players are online, the doll spends durability to send half of damage you receive to its bound target. A ward or Hex Guard Doll on that target can prevent the transfer.
manual.warlockery.conjuration.doll_guard: Use in the air to bind this doll to yourself, or use it on another player to bind them. Keep it in the bound player's inventory or a loaded Doll Shelf. It spends durability to preserve another protection doll during activation or hostile corruption.
manual.warlockery.conjuration.armor_mend: Use in the air to bind this doll to yourself, or use it on another player to bind them. Keep it in that player's inventory or a loaded Doll Shelf. While its bound player is online, it periodically spends one doll durability to repair two durability on damaged worn armor.
manual.warlockery.codex.bucketspirit:
The Cauldron Flowing Spirit working in this book uses one bucket of Water, an empty Bucket, a Congealed Spirit, Subdued Spirit, Whiff of Magic, and 1200 altar power. This working only runs in the Spirit World. Use the filled bucket on the top of a block to pour a source; use an empty Bucket on that source to collect it again.

Ordinary living creatures touching Flowing Spirit receive Regeneration I. Nightmares, undead, and demons receive Weakness II instead. In the Spirit World, a poured source can also complete a correctly built Spirit Portal frame.
manual.warlockery.codex.buckethollowtear:
The Distilling Condensed Fear working in the Distilling book produces a Hollow Tears Bucket from a Spirit Bucket, Oil of Vitriol, and two Clay Jars. Use the filled bucket on the top of a block to pour a source; use an empty Bucket on that source to collect it again.

Undead and demons touching Hollow Tears heal 2 health and receive Resistance I. Players touching it receive Weakness II and Mining Fatigue I. Other living creatures receive neither response.
manual.warlockery.codex.bucketerosionbre:
Throw a Brew of Erosion into a replaceable space to create Erosion fluid, then use an empty Bucket on its source to collect an Erosion Brew Bucket. Use the filled bucket on the top of a block to pour it again.

Every living creature touching this fluid takes 2 magic damage, suffers one durability wear on each damageable equipped item, and receives the Erosion burden. Continued contact can repeat the damage and wear.
manual.warlockery.codex.bucketbrew.title: Colored Brew Water Bucket: Use
manual.warlockery.codex.bucketbrew:
The Cauldron Colored Brew Water working in this book combines one bucket of Water, an empty Bucket, a Brew of Combustion, and a dye. Use the filled bucket on the top of a block to pour a source; use an empty Bucket on that source to collect it again.

Colored Brew Water has no direct contact effect in the world. Use it only in a machine working that explicitly requests it; standing in it does not apply a brew effect.
manual.warlockery.conjuration.ingredient: Concentrated Bat Ball: Use

Craft a Concentrated Bat Ball from eight bat-binding fibers around a Slimeball. Use it on a bat to capture that bat; one ball holds up to eight. Use a filled ball normally in open space to release every stored bat at once. The tooltip shows its current count.
manual.warlockery.conjuration.spectralst: Create this focus with the Rite of Necromancy: Spectral Stone. Use it on a spectral creature to capture it, then use the filled stone normally to release one spirit ahead of you. A stone holds up to three creatures of one species and will not mix species. A released mob is bound to you. The Rite of Binding: Spectral Stone can capture nearby spirits into it as a group.
manual.warlockery.conjuration.ingredient: Subdued Spirit: Use

Defeat a free Spirit to collect a Subdued Spirit. Crouch and use it on a bell inside a recognized village to create a Subdued Village Spirit. This consumes one raw spirit and records that bell's position and dimension. The bell remains intact. A bell outside a village cannot capture a village spirit.

A raw Subdued Spirit can also answer the Listening Ring in Circle Magic. Drop it into the empty center of a hollow three-by-three ring of eight Ritual Chalk marks, without a Golden Chalk center, and wait three seconds. Stay within 32 blocks. It seeks a village in the Overworld or a Nether fortress in the Nether and reports direction and distance. The item remains intact and no altar charge is required; pick it up and drop it again to repeat. Other dimensions do not answer.
Subdued Village Spirit: Use

Create this bound spirit by using a raw Subdued Spirit on a bell inside a recognized village. Hold the bound spirit and use it to report your distance from the recorded bell. In another dimension it reports that the village lies elsewhere. Reading the distance consumes nothing.

The binding remembers that bell's position and dimension. It does not search for a new village or teleport you. This bound variant does not activate the raw spirit's dropped Listening Ring behavior.
manual.warlockery.conjuration.hornoftheh: Earn the Horn by completing the fifth Werewolf trial: kill a Thorned Pursuer with your own transformed claws. Use the Horn normally with open space two blocks ahead to summon a Thorned Pursuer that answers you. The Horn is consumed unless you have infinite materials.
manual.warlockery.conjuration.ingredient: Fool's Skull

Death may drop a Fool's Skull. Use it normally with open space two blocks ahead to summon your Pale Steed. Use it again while that owned steed is within 64 blocks to dismiss the steed instead. The Skull is reusable.
Necromantic Stone

Create this focus with the Rite of Necromancy: Necromantic Stone. Use it on a creature that can be commanded by necromancy to bind that creature to you, quiet its target, make it persistent, and grant 30 seconds of Resistance. Each successful command costs one durability. A creature already bound to another necromancer refuses.
manual.warlockery.circles.ingredient_way: Craft a Waystone from flint and a Bone Needle. Use a plain Waystone on a block to record the space above it, creating a Bound Waystone. Use it on a living creature instead to create a Blooded Waystone. Circle binding rites and the automatic Veil Chalk circles offer other ways to record or copy a destination.

A Bound Waystone remembers a position and dimension. Use it normally to travel there. Hold Shift and use it on a block to replace its destination with the space above that block. Crossing dimensions requires the Otherwhere path. The item reports success or the missing requirement; keep the arrival space safe and clear.

A Blooded Waystone remembers the living creature on which its plain Waystone was used. Use it normally to check whether that creature can currently be found. It is a sympathetic focus for rites and creature abilities; it does not teleport the holder by itself.
manual.warlockery.herbology.boline.title: Boline: Use
manual.warlockery.herbology.boline: Craft a Boline from two iron ingots and a wooden stick. Use it to break dangerous magical plants without triggering their special harvest defense; it still loses normal tool durability. It also works as shears: use it directly on a ready shearable creature, or use it on blocks that accept shears. The Safe Harvest lesson lists the hazards this avoids.
manual.warlockery.herbology.ingredient_i: Harvest mature Snowbell to obtain Icy Needles. In the Spirit World, use one normally to wake; during a temporary manifestation it returns you to the Spirit World instead. Outside the dream, use one while sleeping, suffering a Waking Nightmare or dream sickness, or near a nightmare creature. It wakes you, clears the nightmare and its Darkness, Nausea, Blindness, and Hunger, removes nearby nightmares, and consumes one needle. Nothing is consumed when no dream trouble is found.
manual.warlockery.herbology.ingredient_w: Grow Wolfsbane from its seeds and harvest the mature crop; werewolves and related lycans can also drop the herb. Use Wolfsbane on a living creature to test for lycanthropy. A positive result consumes one herb and gives Weakness II and Slowness I for 10 seconds. A clear result consumes nothing. Wolfsbane also serves werewolf rites and brews.
manual.warlockery.brew.kettle_recipe:
Making this brew
Use a Kettle for this fixed recipe. The Runed Cauldron's configurable mixtures use a separate system, explained in Waking the Cauldron.
manual.warlockery.machine_setup.spirit_w:
Spirit World only
This Spirit Bucket recipe works only in the Spirit World. A correctly filled, heated and powered Runed Cauldron in the Overworld will not start it. Read Crossing the Dreaming Gate and The Silver Cord in Warlockery: Conjuration and Fetishes for entry and inventory rules. Circle Magic remains unavailable in the Spirit World.
manual.warlockery.machine_setup.bodega:
Required familiar: Owl
Keep a living Owl bound to you within 16 blocks of the Kettle. Open the Kettle yourself and remain nearby as its brewer. An unbound Owl or one owned by someone else cannot satisfy this recipe. Use the Rite of Binding: Familiar instructions to prepare your companion.
manual.warlockery.machine_setup.cursed_l:
Required familiar: Familiar Cat
Keep a living Familiar Cat bound to you within 16 blocks of the Kettle. Open the Kettle yourself and remain nearby as its brewer. An ordinary Cat, an unbound familiar, or another player's familiar cannot satisfy this recipe. The Rite of Binding: Familiar explains how to turn an eligible Cat into your bound Familiar Cat.
manual.warlockery.machine_setup.frogs_to:
Required familiar: Toad
Keep a living Toad bound to you within 16 blocks of the Kettle. Open the Kettle yourself and remain nearby as its brewer. An ordinary Frog, an unbound Toad, or another player's Toad cannot satisfy this recipe. The Rite of Binding: Familiar explains how to turn an eligible Frog into your bound Toad.
manual.warlockery.machine_setup.drain_gr:
Prepare partly grown crops near the Brazier; newly planted crops with no growth cannot be drained. Keep wounded undead within 3 blocks if you want the healing benefit. Each successful drain removes one crop growth stage and restores 10% of nearby wounded undead creatures' maximum health.

The starting burn lasts 60 seconds. Every drained crop stage adds 40 seconds, so a growing field can keep it burning much longer. Keep the Wood Ash inside while it burns. Use a Water Bucket or Water Bottle on the Brazier to extinguish it and clear its contents.
manual.warlockery.ritual.setup.hell_on_e: The 5,000 altar power listed above pays only for opening the breach. After casting, the breach consumes another 200 altar power per second from the casting circle's altar supply. Leave enough stored reserve and recharge to support it: a failed upkeep payment closes the breach. An extra bound Waystone can move the breach, but power is still drawn near the original casting circle.
manual.warlockery.brew.behavior.grow: Throw the brew over crops, saplings or other plants that accept bone meal. It repeatedly stimulates their growth in one burst, up to 32 growth steps per position; plants that no longer accept bone meal stop growing.
manual.warlockery.brew.behavior.extingui: Throw the brew at fire or burning creatures. It clears fire from living creatures in reach, removes fire blocks, and puts out lit campfires, candles and candle cakes.
manual.warlockery.brew.behavior.freeze: Throw the brew at creatures or a pool of still water. It extinguishes creatures and sharply increases their freezing buildup, and changes replaceable water source blocks into ice. Flowing water is unchanged.
manual.warlockery.brew.behavior.place_we: Throw the brew at a supported surface to cover nearby replaceable spaces with cobwebs. Each web needs a sturdy block directly beneath it; solid occupied spaces are skipped.
manual.warlockery.brew.behavior.ignite: Throw the brew at creatures or flammable surroundings. Creatures in reach burn for 6 seconds multiplied by potency, and nearby replaceable spaces catch fire wherever fire can survive. Keep yourself outside the splash if you do not want to burn.
manual.warlockery.brew.behavior.explode: Throw the brew at the point you want to blast. It immediately causes an explosion whose strength rises with potency, damaging nearby creatures and affecting terrain according to the world's explosion rules.
manual.warlockery.brew.behavior.push: Throw the brew beside the creatures you want to scatter. Living creatures in reach receive an outward shove away from the impact point, with a small upward lift. Potency controls the shove, and the thrower can also be caught.
manual.warlockery.brew.behavior.pull: Throw the brew where you want nearby creatures to gather. Living creatures in reach are pulled toward the impact point with a small upward lift. Potency controls the pull, and the thrower can also be caught.
manual.warlockery.brew.behavior.lift: Throw the brew at a creature's feet to launch living creatures in reach upward. Potency controls the initial lift, and the impact clears their accumulated fall distance; it does not provide lasting protection from the next fall.
manual.warlockery.brew.behavior.attract_: Throw the brew where you want nearby animals to go. It directs animals in reach toward the impact point using their normal pathfinding, so they still need a route they can traverse.
manual.warlockery.brew.behavior.repel_an: Throw the brew near unwanted animals. It stops their current path and shoves them away from the impact point; potency controls the strength of the shove.
manual.warlockery.brew.behavior.fell_log: Throw the brew near a tree trunk or other connected logs. It starts at the nearest log in reach and breaks connected logs with drops, including diagonal connections. One burst breaks up to 64 logs multiplied by potency, with a limit of 256, so connected wooden structures can be affected too.
manual.warlockery.brew.behavior.prune_le: Throw the brew into foliage to break leaf blocks throughout its reach and release their normal drops. It affects placed leaves as well as naturally grown foliage.
manual.warlockery.brew.behavior.waste: Throw the brew at enemies or foliage. Players in reach receive Hunger II for 60 seconds, hostile monsters receive Wither II for 30 seconds, and nearby leaves break with drops. Players caught in their own splash are affected too.
manual.warlockery.brew.behavior.harvest_: Throw the brew over ripe crops. Mature crops release their harvest and reset to their youngest growth stage. Immature crops are skipped; recognized crop blocks without a growth-age property are broken and drop their harvest.
manual.warlockery.brew.behavior.till_soi: Throw the brew over dirt or grass with empty space above it. Eligible dirt-family blocks become farmland. Clear blocks above the soil first where tilling fails.
manual.warlockery.brew.behavior.reveal: Throw the brew near a creature hidden by invisibility. It clears the creature's invisibility and Invisibility effect, then gives it a glowing outline for 15 seconds. Creatures that are already visible are unchanged.
manual.warlockery.brew.behavior.remove_b: Throw the brew at creatures whose beneficial potion effects you want to dispel. It immediately removes their active beneficial effects throughout the splash area, including your own if you stand within reach.
manual.warlockery.brew.behavior.remove_h: Throw the brew at creatures suffering unwanted potion effects. It immediately removes active effects that are not classified as beneficial. This clears potion effects; separate ritual hexes and persistent brew curses need their own cures.
manual.warlockery.brew.behavior.remove_n: Throw the brew at a creature suffering Nausea to remove that potion effect immediately. It does nothing to a creature without Nausea.
manual.warlockery.brew.behavior.harm_wer: Throw the brew at a werewolf, Lycan Villager or player afflicted with lycanthropy. Eligible werewolf targets take dedicated anti-werewolf damage equal to 10 health points multiplied by potency, before their damage rules are applied.
manual.warlockery.brew.behavior.weaken_v: Throw the brew at a vampire or player afflicted with vampirism. Eligible vampire targets receive Weakness III for 60 seconds. Ordinary creatures in the same splash are unaffected by this working.
manual.warlockery.brew.behavior.harm_dem: Throw the brew at demons such as imps, the Emberhorn Archfiend or the Abyssal Regent. Eligible demon targets take 12 health points of magic damage multiplied by potency, before defenses are applied.
manual.warlockery.brew.behavior.summon_b: Throw the brew into an open area to summon ordinary bats around the impact point. Potency determines the number requested, from 2 to 12; these bats are not bound to you or assigned an attack target by the brew.
manual.warlockery.brew.behavior.summon_m: Throw the brew near hostile monsters or another survival player to summon a flock of Hex Bats bound to you. Potency requests 3 to 8 bats. Their initial target must be eligible: they spare you, your owned creatures, passive animals, villagers, golems, witches, other Hex Bats and Warlockery's arcane creatures.
manual.warlockery.brew.behavior.blight: Throw the brew over vegetation or nearby beasts, villagers and wandering traders. It destroys affected crops, flowers, leaves and saplings without harvesting them, turns affected soils into dirt, and gives eligible creatures Wither I for 15 seconds and Weakness II for 30 seconds.
manual.warlockery.brew.behavior.erode: Throw the brew at stonework or enemies. It removes susceptible stone, cobblestone and terracotta; obsidian breaks with drops. Creatures in reach take magic damage and immediate equipment wear, followed by further equipment wear each second for 30 seconds. A replaceable impact space fills with Erosion fluid, which continues hurting creatures and wearing their equipment while they stand in it.
manual.warlockery.brew.behavior.fear: Throw the brew near creatures you want to drive away. It shoves affected creatures away from the impact point; affected mobs abandon their target and repeatedly try to flee that point for 60 seconds. An ordinary thrown splash spares its thrower.
manual.warlockery.brew.behavior.pull_to_: Throw the brew near a creature you want to draw toward yourself. Affected creatures are pulled toward the thrower's position, with a small upward lift. The thrown splash spares its thrower; without an owner, the pull leads to the impact point instead.
manual.warlockery.brew.behavior.place_li: Throw the brew over still water to grow lily pads on nearby water source blocks. The space above each source must be replaceable and suitable for a lily pad. Flowing water cannot support this working.
manual.warlockery.brew.behavior.ice_shel: Throw the brew at the center of the area you want to enclose. It forms a hollow shell of packed ice in replaceable spaces and water around the impact, with a radius based on the brew's reach. Solid obstructions remain, so they can leave gaps in the shell.
manual.warlockery.brew.behavior.place_sn: Throw the brew over ground you want covered in snow. It places snow layers in nearby replaceable spaces wherever snow can survive, leaving unsuitable surfaces unchanged.
manual.warlockery.brew.behavior.harm_ins: Throw the brew at spiders, silverfish or other creatures vulnerable to Bane of Arthropods. Eligible targets take 12 health points of magic damage multiplied by potency, before defenses are applied.
manual.warlockery.brew.behavior.level_la: Throw the brew at the height you want to level around. In nearby columns it removes eligible terrain above the block beneath the impact and fills lower columns up to that height using their existing surface material. It stops at unsuitable blocks or occupied fill spaces; removed terrain is not harvested.
manual.warlockery.brew.behavior.breed_an: Throw the brew among adult animals ready to breed. It puts them in love mode and heals 2 health points; nearby adult villagers receive three bread each and still need their usual breeding conditions. A splash covering pairs of adult zombies already bound to you can also create one bound baby Zombie Villager per pair.
manual.warlockery.brew.behavior.pulveriz: Throw the brew at stone or sandstone. Stone becomes cobblestone, deepslate becomes cobbled deepslate, and cobblestone becomes gravel. Sandstone and red sandstone become their matching sand; other eligible rock becomes gravel. These are block transformations rather than harvested drops.
manual.warlockery.brew.behavior.raise_la: Throw the brew near the ground you want to raise. It finds eligible terrain in nearby columns and copies each column's uppermost eligible block into the replaceable space immediately above it, raising that surface by one block.
manual.warlockery.brew.behavior.buff_und: Throw the brew over undead already bound to you. They receive Strength II and Resistance I for 60 seconds, plus Undead Mending for 30 seconds. Undead Mending restores one health point every 2.5 seconds. The working needs a living thrower and affects only that thrower's owned undead, or the thrower if the thrower is recognized as undead.
manual.warlockery.brew.behavior.spread_h: Throw the brew where an afflicted creature and your intended victims are both in reach. It copies every non-beneficial potion effect from the afflicted creature nearest the impact onto the other nearby living creatures, preserving their remaining durations and strengths. The original creature keeps its effects.
manual.warlockery.brew.behavior.steal_be: Throw the brew at creatures carrying beneficial potion effects. With a living thrower, it removes those effects from other creatures in reach and transfers copies, including their remaining durations and strengths, to the thrower.
manual.warlockery.brew.behavior.place_th: Throw the brew onto dirt or sand near creatures you want to trap. It grows mature berry bushes on suitable soil and cacti on sand, and gives affected creatures Slowness V for 6 seconds while trying to surround their feet with berry bushes. Your bound toad within 16 blocks raises cactus growth from three to four blocks and extends the slowing to 10 seconds.
manual.warlockery.brew.behavior.random_t: Throw the brew at creatures you want to displace. Each living creature in reach gets one attempt to teleport to a random nearby position, including a possible height change. A creature stays put if that destination fails the normal teleport checks; the thrower can be affected too.
manual.warlockery.brew.behavior.transpos: Throw the brew near ore while leaving open space around the impact. It moves up to 32 eligible ore blocks from within reach into replaceable spaces within two blocks of the impact. Their original positions fill with stone, or deepslate below height zero; without destination space, no ore can move.
manual.warlockery.brew.behavior.harm_und: Throw the brew at zombies, skeletons or other creatures vulnerable to Smite. Eligible targets take 12 health points of magic damage multiplied by potency, before defenses are applied.
manual.warlockery.brew.behavior.curse_un: Throw the brew at undead creatures. It ignites affected undead for 30 seconds multiplied by potency and gives them Weakness II for 60 seconds. Fire-immune creatures may resist the burning.
manual.warlockery.brew.behavior.place_vi: Throw the brew against a wall or beside existing hanging vines. It grows connected vines through suitable nearby spaces, starting close to the impact; every section needs a valid wall attachment or supporting vine above. Your bound toad within 16 blocks increases the spread and lets the growth cross wider steps.
manual.warlockery.brew.behavior.dissipat: Throw the brew into gas to remove recognized gas blocks and custom brew gas clouds within reach. It also deals 12 health points of magic damage multiplied by potency to eligible spectral creatures caught in the splash.
manual.warlockery.brew.behavior.drain_re: Throw the brew at a creature carrying magical benefits or compatible powered equipment. It strips beneficial potion effects and extracts up to 50,000 energy units from each supported equipped item; player inventory items are checked too. Items that do not expose extractable energy are unchanged.
manual.warlockery.brew.behavior.extend_e: Throw the brew at creatures with active timed potion effects. It doubles each finite remaining duration, up to a maximum of 30 minutes, preserving effect strength. Harmful effects are extended too, so clear unwanted effects first.
manual.warlockery.brew.behavior.place_wa: Throw the brew into empty or replaceable dry spaces to create water source blocks around the impact. Potency controls how many sources appear. Spaces already containing fluid or solid blocks are skipped.
manual.warlockery.brew.behavior.darkness: Throw the brew at creatures you want to make vulnerable to darkness. The mark lasts 60 seconds. Below light level 5 they take magic damage and receive Darkness and Wither; the mark continues checking each second, so entering darkness later also triggers harm. Move into brighter light to stop those repeated dark-area hits.
manual.warlockery.brew.behavior.moonligh: Throw the brew over creatures with an unobstructed view of the sky while the moon has some brightness. They receive Night Vision and Luck for 2 minutes and Regeneration for 30 seconds. When moon brightness exceeds three quarters, Luck and Regeneration rise from level I to level II.
manual.warlockery.brew.behavior.part_wat: Throw the brew over water sources with replaceable space above them. It turns up to 128 eligible source blocks into frosted ice to make a temporary crossing. The ice follows its normal melting behavior; flowing water is unchanged.
manual.warlockery.brew.behavior.part_lav: Throw the brew over lava sources with replaceable space above them. It replaces up to 96 eligible source blocks with basalt for a crossing. After 20 seconds, unchanged temporary basalt returns to its original lava when the area is loaded, so cross promptly.
manual.warlockery.brew.behavior.plant_dr: Throw near a plantable seed or plant item you dropped beside suitable soil. For each loose item stack it plants one item on the nearest valid ground with replaceable space above, consuming one item only after successful planting. Unsupported plants or unsuitable ground are skipped.
manual.warlockery.brew.behavior.summon_p: Throw the brew near enemies with room around the impact. It attempts to summon four toads and gives nearby living creatures Poison II for 30 seconds, excluding the thrower, frogs and toads. The newly summoned toads are not bound to you by this working.
manual.warlockery.brew.behavior.raise_de: Throw the brew into an area with two blocks of clear space around the impact to raise one to three Corpses. A living thrower becomes their owner. They receive Strength II and Resistance I for 60 seconds and initially attack the nearest nearby non-undead creature other than the thrower.
manual.warlockery.brew.behavior.apply_mo: Throw at your feet or another living target before a fight. For 3 minutes, the affected target takes half damage; an affected player also tires faster and uses more hunger. The protection begins on impact.
manual.warlockery.brew.behavior.apply_ab: Throw at your feet or a living target before a magical attack. For 2 minutes, the brew absorbs three quarters of incoming magical damage. A player with a selected magic path turns the stored energy into reserve, up to four points each second while that path has room.
manual.warlockery.brew.behavior.apply_at: Throw at a living target you want arrows to seek. For 60 seconds, nearby arrows fired by others bend toward that target. The brew attracts dangerous shots; it does not shield the marked creature from their impact.
manual.warlockery.brew.behavior.bottle_y: Throw onto open ground and collect the Glass Bottles that appear at the impact. The number depends on potency: three times the shown potency, rounded up, with a minimum of one bottle and a maximum of eight.
manual.warlockery.brew.behavior.apply_ga: Throw at your feet or a living target before entering brew gas. For 3 minutes, standing with feet or head inside a recognized gas block clears harmful potion effects once each second. This working does not remove the gas blocks.
manual.warlockery.brew.behavior.apply_en: Throw at a living target to suppress its ender travel for 60 seconds. While affected, ender-creature teleports, Ender Pearl travel and Chorus Fruit travel are blocked. It does not promise to stop every other kind of magical journey.
manual.warlockery.brew.behavior.apply_il: Throw at an armored living target. For 60 seconds, each worn armor piece increases the target's renewed Slowness and Mining Fatigue, up to level IV with four pieces. An unarmored target has no armor burden to amplify.
manual.warlockery.brew.behavior.apply_in: Throw at a living target to curse it for 2 minutes. Temporary hostile creatures can appear nearby about every ten seconds while fewer than two remain. They need free space to appear, pursue the cursed target, and disappear after their brief lives.
manual.warlockery.brew.behavior.apply_ke: Throw at your feet or another player before danger. If the affected player dies within 10 minutes, their active potion effects are restored on respawn. It preserves effects through that death; it does not prevent the death itself.

Throw at your feet or another player before danger. If the affected player dies within 10 minutes, their dropped inventory is saved and returned on respawn. Items that cannot fit in the new inventory are dropped beside the respawned player.
manual.warlockery.brew.behavior.apply_ni: Throw at an awake living target to cause waking nightmares for 2 minutes. Temporary hostile creatures can appear about every five seconds, up to three at once, where space is clear. Sleeping pauses new appearances. An Icy Needle can end the waking nightmare.
manual.warlockery.brew.behavior.apply_po: Throw at your feet or another living attacker before combat. For 2 minutes, that attacker poisons living victims when it deals damage. Each hit gives Poison II for eight seconds; merely holding a weapon does not trigger the poison.
manual.warlockery.brew.behavior.apply_re: Throw at your feet or another living target before arrows arrive. For 60 seconds, arrows that hit the protected target reverse direction and become that target's projectiles. The reflection occurs on impact, not when the arrow is fired.

Throw at your feet or another living target before a fight. For 60 seconds, a living attacker receives half the damage it inflicts, bounded between half a point and eight points per hit. The protected target still takes its incoming damage.

Throw at an animal before it dies. If that animal dies within 10 minutes, a replacement animal from the world's reincarnation choices appears at its death position and keeps its custom name. This working does not resurrect players or preserve the animal's old body.

Throw at your feet or another living target before combat. For 60 seconds, living attackers are pushed away whenever they deal damage to the affected target. The shove follows a real hit; it does not cancel the incoming damage.

Throw at your feet or another living target. For 60 seconds, the affected body shrinks to half its normal scale where that creature supports resizing. Its normal size returns when the working expires.
manual.warlockery.brew.behavior.shift_se: Throw at the landscape you want to change. The world day selects a four-day cycle: growth; growth with extinguishing; crop harvest with leaf pruning; then freezing with snow. The nearby biome also changes to an available biome for that season.
manual.warlockery.brew.behavior.summon_a: Throw into a clear space near the intended victim to call an Abyssal Regent just above the impact. It pursues the nearest other living target in reach. The Regent is hostile and is not bound as your companion; an Infernal Animus cannot bind it. Leave yourself an escape route before throwing.
manual.warlockery.brew.behavior.apply_ti: Throw at your feet or another living target. For 60 seconds, the target has a glowing outline and recurring pale teal particles around its body. This working marks the creature visibly; it does not replace a player's skin texture.
manual.warlockery.brew.behavior.apply_we: Throw at a player while that player is in the form you want to preserve. For 10 minutes, the working remembers that current form and restores it if the player changes form. Use it after the desired transformation, not before.
manual.warlockery.brew.behavior.apply_di: Throw at a living target to make it a contagious carrier for 60 seconds. Every two seconds it can infect nearby living creatures, giving them Poison II and Weakness II as well as a shorter contagious period. Keep allies away from the carrier.
manual.warlockery.brew.behavior.apply_in: Throw at a villager to turn it into a zombie villager. Other living targets are briefly immobilized and become contagious for 60 seconds, passing poison and weakness to nearby creatures. The impact also turns nearby stone, cobblestone and stone bricks into infested blocks.
manual.warlockery.brew.behavior.apply_si: Throw at a living target in water or another sinking fluid. For 60 seconds, the affected target is pulled downward and cannot maintain swimming or sprinting in that fluid. On dry ground the sinking burden has no fluid to act through.
manual.warlockery.brew.behavior.apply_su: Throw at an undead creature vulnerable to Smite. For 2 minutes, direct daytime sky exposure repeatedly burns and damages it. Shelter from the sky, nighttime or Fire Resistance prevents this burning; ordinary living targets do not receive the curse.
manual.warlockery.brew.behavior.apply_vo: Throw at a living target, then deal damage to trigger the working. The next damaging hit within 10 minutes makes the target explode once. This blast harms nearby creatures but does not destroy terrain; the volatile charge is spent by the blast.
manual.warlockery.brew.behavior.summon_o: Throw into clear space near an enemy to call three owls bound to the thrower. They select a nearby hostile creature or a creature attacking the thrower, while avoiding the thrower's owned allies. Without an eligible enemy they still appear, but have no chosen victim.
manual.warlockery.brew.behavior.apply_cu: Throw at a living target standing on the ground. For 60 seconds, the curse launches it upward and sideways about every two seconds when it is grounded. The jumps happen on their own; an airborne target waits until it lands for the next launch.
manual.warlockery.brew.behavior.apply_ov: Throw at a living target in a hot biome. For 60 seconds, a dry target without Fire Resistance repeatedly catches fire and takes heat damage. Water, rain or Fire Resistance prevents this burning while the curse remains active.
manual.warlockery.brew.behavior.apply_sl: Throw at your feet or another player to enter the Spirit World, leaving a sleeping body behind. The working also renews Slowness and Darkness for up to five minutes. Read Crossing the Dreaming Gate in Warlockery: Conjuration and Fetishes first, and use an Icy Needle for a deliberate return. Surrounding dream influences can cause nightmares.
manual.warlockery.brew.behavior.apply_sn: Throw at your feet or another living target, then move across ground that can support snow. For 60 seconds, snow is laid near the target's feet once each second where the space is replaceable. Solid obstacles are not replaced.
manual.warlockery.brew.behavior.sprout_b: Throw toward open space while facing the direction you want a branch bridge to grow. Branches extend forward from the impact and rise gradually, with leaves along the path. Existing solid blocks and containers are not replaced.
manual.warlockery.brew.behavior.substitu: Throw beside a dropped stack of the replacement building block. The nearest suitable existing block type becomes the target for substitution; matching blocks in reach are replaced, consuming one dropped item per block changed, up to 64. Containers and unsupported replacements are skipped.
manual.warlockery.brew.behavior.apply_de: Throw at a living target to reverse its breathing needs for 3 minutes. Deep enough in water, its air refills; outside that water, its air drains until it takes drowning damage. Stay mostly submerged if you use this on yourself.
manual.warlockery.brew.behavior.apply_gr: Throw at your feet or another living target. For 60 seconds, nearby creatures that fear the grotesque stop targeting and try to flee from the affected body. Creatures immune to this fear stand their ground, and blocked paths may prevent escape.
manual.warlockery.brew.behavior.solidify: Throw into placed Hollow Tears to turn that fluid into Stone within the brew's reach. Ordinary water and dry terrain are not this working's material; first place Hollow Tears where you want the stone to form.

Throw into placed Hollow Tears to turn that fluid into Dirt within the brew's reach. Ordinary water and dry terrain are not this working's material; first place Hollow Tears where you want the dirt to form.
Throw into placed Hollow Tears to turn that fluid into Sand within the brew's reach. Provide support beneath the new sand if you want it to stay in place. Ordinary water is not converted.

Throw into placed Hollow Tears to turn that fluid into Sandstone within the brew's reach. Ordinary water and dry terrain are not this working's material; first place Hollow Tears where you want the sandstone to form.

Throw into placed Hollow Tears to erode breakable blocks in columns beneath that fluid, reaching up to 32 blocks downward. Containers and unbreakable blocks stop a column. The working leaves the Hollow Tears itself in place and can open a deep hole below it.
manual.warlockery.infusions.earmuffs:
Wear Earmuffs in your head slot. Hold them and use them to put them on, or move them into that armor slot. While worn, they clear Blindness and Nausea about once each second.

Put them on before facing a creature or brew that clouds your senses. An effect may appear briefly before the next clearing. Earmuffs do not remove every potion effect or end a lasting ritual hex.
manual.warlockery.infusions.seepingshoes:
Wear Seeping Shoes in your feet slot. When Poison afflicts you, the shoes remove it and send a burst of growth into nearby plants that accept bone meal. Stand beside young crops or saplings, within about three blocks, to put that poison to use.

The growth happens when poison is removed, not simply because you are walking. Plants already fully grown have nothing to gain. The shoes also carry Depth Strider III, helping you move through water.
manual.warlockery.infusions.barkbelt:
Wear the Bark Belt in your legs slot. Standing on grass, dirt, moss or other living ground grants Absorption II, shown as four extra golden hearts. These hearts absorb incoming damage before your normal health.

The belt checks the block beneath your feet about once each second. Stone floors do not sustain the blessing, and it fades shortly after you leave living ground. The belt does not make a dangerous fall harmless once those extra hearts are spent.
manual.warlockery.infusions.twisting_ban:
Wear the Twisting Band in your head slot, then look directly at a living creature within about twelve blocks. A clear line of sight lets your gaze renew Weakness II and Slowness I on the creature. Looking away stops renewing them.

Another player who stares directly at you from nearby is turned away and loses hunger. This part needs another player; it is not triggered by a cow or other ordinary creature.
manual.warlockery.infusions.iceslippers:
Wear Icy Slippers in your feet slot to use their Frost Walker II enchantment. Walk from solid shore beside still water, keeping your feet level with the water's surface. Nearby water freezes into a temporary path as you move.

The water needs clear air above it. Swimming inside the pool or riding a creature does not activate this crossing. The ice can melt, so do not depend on it as a permanent bridge.
manual.warlockery.infusions.forgewardens:
Wear the Forgewarden's Girdle in your legs slot and leave your attacking hand empty. A barehanded hit deals at least four health points of damage and knocks the victim upward. Holding a weapon prevents this barehanded benefit.

When another player wearing a Stonebroker's Quiver stands within about twelve blocks, both wearers gain Resistance I. The pairing needs two players wearing the complementary pieces.
manual.warlockery.infusions.stonebrokers:
Wear the Stonebroker's Quiver in your chest slot, then draw and release a bow normally. It supplies ordinary arrows even when you carry none. Arrows you fire while wearing it travel faster and give a struck living target Weakness I for ten seconds.

The quiver's shots deal extra damage to airborne targets. A nearby player wearing a Forgewarden's Girdle also shares a Resistance I blessing with you. Special ammunition keeps its own supply requirements.
manual.warlockery.infusions.deathscowl:
Wear Death's Hood in your head slot. At night it renews Night Vision. Look directly at a living creature within about ten blocks and with a clear line of sight to renew Slowness II on it.

For Death's complete disguise, combine the hood with Death's Robe and Death's Feet and carry the Hand of Death. The Hand of Death entry explains the scythe transformation and its hunger cost.
manual.warlockery.infusions.deathsrobe:
Wear Death's Robe in your chest slot. It renews Fire Resistance I about once each second, protecting you from fire and lava damage while the effect remains active. Wait for the effect to appear before entering danger.

The robe is one part of Death's disguise, together with Death's Hood, Death's Feet and the Hand of Death. The full outfit enables the hand's scythe transformation; the robe's fire protection works on its own.
manual.warlockery.infusions.deathsfeet:
Wear Death's Feet as boots in your feet slot. Their Frost Walker II enchantment creates temporary ice when you walk from shore beside still water, and Fire Protection IV reduces fire damage. The boots work as footwear without a separate use action.

They also complete Death's disguise when worn with Death's Hood and Death's Robe while carrying the Hand of Death. Use the hand to change its form once the outfit is complete; the boots do not perform that transformation themselves.
manual.warlockery.infusions.deathshand:
Hold the Hand of Death while wearing Death's Hood, Death's Robe and Death's Feet, then use the hand to change it into its scythe form. Use it again to change back. Missing outfit pieces prevent this change.

Keeping the scythe active with the complete outfit consumes one hunger point each second. Change it back when you are done fighting. Independently of that transformation, hits from the Hand of Death deal at least 15% of the victim's maximum health before the victim's own defenses and damage rules apply.
manual.warlockery.infusions.arcane_focus:
Use the focus on a chalk circle's center to open its ritual choices and missing requirements. Away from a circle, it directs your selected infusion: use in the air for a personal power, on a living creature for a targeted power, or on a block for a working at that place.

First acquire an infusion and enough of its personal reserve. With more than one active path, crouch-use the focus in the air to cycle paths; the message identifies the new selection. On creatures and blocks, crouch-use requests an alternate action where that path offers one. An invalid target or insufficient reserve refuses the working without spending reserve. The Infusion Recharge rite restores reserve.

Personal powers include Fire Resistance for Imp magic, the current sacrifice power for Infernal, Night Vision for Grave, Invisibility for Light, a short forward teleport for Otherwhere, an Overworld shockwave, and a Sky launch. Light can imprison a creature or build a temporary wall. Sky lifts a creature or makes an updraft at a block. Grave binds undead and directs them to a clicked block; its drink and costs are explained on the Infused Brew of the Grave page.

Select the required path first, using the Arcane Focus page's controls. With Imp, use on another creature to ignite it for ten seconds; crouch-use grants it one minute of Fire Resistance instead. Use on a block to remove nearby water; waterlogged blocks themselves are removed as well.

With Infernal, crouch-use on an eligible unbound mob to enthrall it. Crouch-use that owned mob again to sacrifice it, removing the creature and taking its kind of power for your personal use. Ordinary use on a mob directs your nearby thralls to attack that target. Use on a block to direct your thralls there. Immune creatures refuse enthrallment.

With Otherwhere, use on a block face to teleport into the adjacent space, which needs two empty blocks above solid support. Crouch-use a block to store your own current position as a recall point. If Otherwhere is your only active path, crouch-use in the air to return there; with several paths, that control cycles selection. Ordinary use on a creature raises both of you eight blocks. Crouch-use on another player takes both of you to your saved recall point.

With Overworld, use on a creature wearing metal armor to knock it away; crouch-use on one holding metal equipment to disarm it. Use on earth or stone to raise matching blocks above it, leaving room for the column. Use on a suitable ore to release its materials and replace it with Stone. Crouch-use an earth block to launch it along your aim; crouch-use another block to draw nearby loose metal items toward you. The Arcane Focus and Grave Brew pages cover Light, Sky and Grave workings.
manual.warlockery.infusions.ingredient_b:
The Grave brew infusion rite in this chapter produces this drink. Finish drinking it to gain the Grave path for two hours. The active path refreshes Night Vision. Select Grave with an Arcane Focus; if several paths are active, crouch-use the focus in the air until Grave is selected.

Use the focus in the air to grant one minute of Night Vision for 4 reserve. Use it on an undead mob to bind that creature for 10 reserve, clearing its current attack target. An ordinary living animal or another player cannot be bound this way. The bond lasts up to two hours and depends on your Grave attunement remaining active.

Use the focus on a block to direct your bound undead nearby toward that position for 5 reserve. Keep your followers within 32 blocks on each axis; the command refuses when no eligible follower is nearby. Bound undead can also answer your recent attacks and attackers. Killing a nourishing creature, including a villager or ordinary animal, yourself or through a Grave-bound mob restores two hearts, food and 4 Grave reserve. The Infusion Recharge rite can refill spent reserve.
manual.warlockery.symbology.mysticbranch:
The Mystic Branch casts named signs directly. Crouch-use it to cycle the selected sign; watch the sign's name in the message. Use without crouching in the air, on a living creature, or on a block according to that sign's target. A chalk circle's center opens ritual choices before branch casting. The Signs and Targets page lists the valid targets.

You need an active selected infusion. Most signs spend 2 of its reserve. Abyssal Banishment, Agony and Dominate also require Infernal attunement. Ravenous Communion instead takes two hearts from you and restores 12 reserve to the selected path.

Four signs must first be unlocked on that particular branch. Carry the matching soul brew in your inventory when casting: Soul of Anguish Demon for Soulfire Lance, Soul of Hunger Demon for Ravenous Communion, Soul of Fear Demon for Dread Sigil, and Soul of Torment Demon for Abyssal Banishment. Unlocking consumes one matching brew and is remembered by that branch. A missing infusion, locked soul sign or insufficient reserve causes refusal.

Holding a Mystic Branch in either hand also deflects incoming projectiles. This protection does not spend casting reserve. The Mystic Branch infusion rite is listed in Infusing Magic.

Use in the air: Grasp of Air draws loose items toward you; Ravenous Communion trades two hearts for reserve; Calm Skies clears rain and thunder. Awaken clears Slowness, Weakness, Nausea, Blindness and Poison. Mend Flesh heals two hearts and adds exhaustion to a player. Awaken and Mend Flesh can also be used on another living creature.

Use on blocks: Sentinel Ward places a protective ward; Dread Sigil places a sanctity ward. Wellspring places water beside the clicked face, Kindle places fire, and Witchlight places magical light. Leave replaceable space with suitable support. Unseal and Seal change a block's open state where it has one. Delve breaks and drops an ordinary breakable block, leaving containers and other blocks that hold information intact. Snuff Light breaks nearby light sources such as torches, lanterns and glowstone, dropping their usual materials; use it on a block or in the air.

Use on living creatures: Soulfire Lance burns and harms its target and nearby creatures; Abyssal Banishment sends a living creature other than a player to the Abyss. Bewilder causes Nausea; Agony deals magic damage; Disarm drops the target's held item; Repulse knocks it away; Hobble slows it. Dominate quiets a mob and draws it toward you with Weakness; Stun inflicts strong Slowness and Weakness. Dread Sigil can also center its ward on a creature. Check the Mystic Branch page for infusion, soul and reserve requirements.
manual.warlockery.conjuration.louse:
Use an empty hand on a living Parasytic Louse to gather it as an item, keeping any stored potion effect. The summoning rite in this chapter provides a way to call the creature.

To load the item, hold the louse in one hand and a potion in the other, then use the louse while aiming into the air. It stores the potion's first effect, including its strength and duration. One potion is consumed and a Glass Bottle is returned. A loaded louse refuses a second potion until its charge has been spent.

Keep the loaded louse in one of your nine hotbar slots. When damage reaches you, a beneficial stored effect goes to you; a harmful effect goes to the living attacker. A harmful charge waits if there is no living attacker. Only the first loaded louse in hotbar order responds to a damage event. The charge is emptied after injection, leaving the louse available to reload.

Use the item on a block face to release a living louse into the adjacent space instead. Leave room for the creature. Successful release consumes the item and carries its stored effect into the creature.
manual.warlockery.conjuration.archfiends:
A player-killed Emberhorn Archfiend can drop an Archfiend's Urn. The chance is 20% without Looting, rising to 30%, 40% and 50% with Looting I, II and III. Prepare for repeated fights; a kill does not guarantee an urn.

The Hex of Hell on Earth in this chapter opens a Hell Rift that can call Emberhorn Archfiends among its randomly chosen demons. Cast it at night in the Overworld. Prepare 8 Ritual Chalk, 12 Infernal Chalk and 16 Veil Chalk marks, plus the circle's heart. The rite consumes a Redstone Soup, Demon Heart, Waystone, Nether Star and one Villager, takes thirteen seconds to cast, and spends 5,000 altar power to open. Read its ritual page for the layout and offering checks.

Keep the casting altar supplied: the open rift consumes 200 power each second and attempts another random demon spawn every three seconds. An extra bound Waystone in the same dimension moves the breach to its stored place; power still comes from the casting circle. A missed upkeep payment closes the breach. Fight the hostile Emberhorn yourself for its urn drop. The Brew of Summon Abyssal Regent calls a different demon and does not provide this urn.

Hold the urn in one hand and a finished brew in the other, then crouch-use the urn in the air to store that brew, consuming one bottle. It stores up to four distinct brew kinds; duplicates and a full urn refuse another addition. Use the urn without crouching to cast all stored brews at the point you are aiming toward, up to 24 blocks away. The stored brews remain, and each cast starts a three-second cooldown. An empty urn cannot cast.
manual.warlockery.circles.circletalisman:
Drop an empty Circle Talisman within six blocks of the prepared circle's center and perform the Bind Circle rite. The talisman captures the chalk pattern and removes the captured chalk from the ground. Pick up the filled talisman before moving to the new site.

Use the filled talisman on a block face to restore the pattern. The space immediately beyond that face becomes the circle's center. For a floor circle, click the top of the floor beneath the desired center. The original offsets and orientation are preserved.

Every glyph needs replaceable space, proper support and a position inside the world's bounds. One blocked glyph prevents the entire restoration and leaves the stored pattern intact; clear the reported obstruction and try again. Success restores every glyph and empties the talisman for another binding. It restores chalk, so arrange the required altar and offerings for the next rite separately.
manual.warlockery.conjuration.rowanwoodd:
Placing a Rowan Wood Door grants a key bound to that door. If your inventory is full, collect the key dropped beside it. Carry a matching Rowan Door Key or Rowan Keyring anywhere in your inventory, then use either half of the door to open or close it.

A blank single Rowan Door Key can bind to a clicked door when you have no matching key. Use it again after binding to open the door. A bound single key cannot be reassigned to a different door. A keyring learns doors by combining bound keys, not by clicking an unknown door.

Redstone closes an open door when a signal arrives; it does not provide an unlocking key. Keep the matching key when dismantling your door: breaking it without permission yields sticks instead of the normal door drop.
manual.warlockery.conjuration.ingredient: Rowan Door Key

A placed Rowan Wood Door gives its placer a key for that door. Keep the key in your inventory to use either half of the matching door. The binding remembers both the door's position and its dimension.

Use an unbound single key on a door for which you have no matching key to bind it, then use the door again to open it. A key already bound elsewhere refuses reassignment. To collect several door permissions into one item, use a Rowan Keyring with bound keys in the opposite hand; the Keyring page explains the exchange.
Rowan Keyring

Hold the keyring in one hand and a bound Rowan Door Key or another bound Rowan Keyring in the opposite hand. Use the receiving keyring in the air to combine the remembered doors. The source key or ring is consumed outside Creative mode. The receiving ring retains its existing doors and adds the new ones without a fixed capacity limit.

An empty source refuses. A source containing only doors already in the receiving ring also refuses and remains intact. Carry the completed ring anywhere in your inventory to open its matching Rowan Wood Doors. Clicking an unfamiliar door with an empty ring cannot bind that door; use a single key first.
manual.warlockery.immortal.bloodcrucible:
As a vampire, use a full Glass Goblet, Warm Blood or raw meat on the crucible to heal four hearts, restore 25 blood and gain ten seconds of Regeneration II. A goblet empties; another offering is consumed. An empty goblet cannot feed it. Mortals cannot receive this blessing.

At vampire level ten, fill your personal blood reserve completely to 3,500. Use a Bone for Teleport, a Water Artichoke Globe for Call Storm, or Wool of Bat for Summon Bats. This consumes one ingredient and all your stored blood, selects that power and grants five charges. Charging replaces the stored charges of the other crucible powers.

Activate the selected power with the Use Supernatural Power control. If a power ingredient is refused, check your vampire level and full blood reserve before trying again. The crucible uses your blood reserve; it has no blood tank to fill beforehand.
manual.warlockery.immortal.coffinblock:
Use a placed Coffin with an empty hand during daylight as a vampire to set your respawn point and bring on night. Rest heals three hearts and grants ten seconds of Regeneration I. The coffin refuses to skip time that is already night. Mortals cannot rest this way.

Use a Sympathetic Vial or Glass Goblet on the coffin to collect your own sample instead. The goblet also fills with blood. Anyone can take this sample, even at night, without paying health. Put the container away before trying to rest: sampling takes priority over the resting action.
manual.warlockery.immortal.glassgoblet:
Use an empty goblet on a living creature to fill it with a sympathetic sample and deal one heart of damage. A vampire can instead crouch-use an empty goblet in the air to take their own blood, losing one heart without falling below half a heart.

Use a full goblet in the air as a vampire to drink: heal three hearts and restore 30 blood, leaving it empty. Mortals cannot drink it to become vampires. A full goblet can also feed a Blood Crucible. Using a goblet on a Coffin takes your own sample and fills it without paying health.

A full goblet used on a creature attempts vampire creation instead of drinking. During the level-nine creation trial, completely drain and mesmerize the target, carry at least 125 blood, and offer a full goblet bound to your own blood. Keep a Coffin within four blocks horizontally and close to the target's level. A player target must have no supernatural form and must crouch to consent. Success empties the goblet and spends 125 blood. Read the level-nine trial before attempting this rite of creation.
manual.warlockery.symbology.mirrorblock:
These placed Mirrors share their workings, including the second Mirror design and the Mirror Surface. Use one with an empty hand to hear whom it judges fairest nearby and recall earlier visitors. It judges nearby living creatures by health, absorption and armor.

Crouch-use with an empty hand to travel to the nearest loaded mirror within 16 blocks in the same dimension. Leave two clear blocks above the destination. Pairing is automatic and costs no altar power. Without a usable partner, the mirror instead releases a hostile Glass Doppelganger above itself if there is room.

Use a handheld Mirror on the surface to bind that tool's return point above it. Use a Quartz Sphere with 500 available altar power nearby to consume the sphere and receive one Replication Charge. Insufficient power leaves the sphere intact.

A bound sympathetic sample used on the surface changes your displayed name to the sample's owner. Your own sample restores your name. This consumes the sample item, including a goblet used as the sample. Other held items refuse unless they are accepted mirror tools.
manual.warlockery.symbology.mirrorblock2:
This Mirror uses the same controls and pairs with either placed Mirror design or a Mirror Surface. The Placed Mirror page in this chapter explains its workings.

Crouch-use with an empty hand travels to the nearest usable mirror within 16 blocks in this dimension; keep two clear blocks above the destination. If no usable partner exists, it summons a hostile Glass Doppelganger instead. Ordinary empty-hand use reports visitors. Quartz Spheres with 500 altar power become Replication Charges, and using a bound sympathetic sample consumes it to borrow its owner's displayed name.
manual.warlockery.symbology.mirrorwall:
The Mirror Surface shares the controls of both placed Mirror designs. It can be their automatic travel partner within 16 blocks in the same dimension. Leave two clear blocks above the destination.

Use an empty hand for the mirror's reading. Crouch-use with an empty hand to travel; without a usable partner, this calls a hostile Glass Doppelganger instead. Use a handheld Mirror to bind its return point. A Quartz Sphere and 500 available altar power make one Replication Charge. A bound sympathetic sample is consumed to borrow its owner's displayed name. The Placed Mirror page gives the complete instructions.
manual.warlockery.herbology.ingredient_v:
Use Verdant Catalyst directly on a flower, sapling or leaf block to replace that block with a randomly chosen magical plant. Each successful transformation consumes one catalyst. Ordinary crops and bare ground do not accept this version.

Possible plants include Embermoss, Glintweed, Leaping Lily, Spanish Moss, Hexwood growth, Bramble, Blood Rose, Critter Snare, Grassper and Wispy Cotton. The Spirit World also adds Nether Wart to the possibilities. Prepare suitable planting space and expect a random result. Prime Verdant Catalyst accepts more targets and has reliable soil conversions, described on its own page.

Use Prime Verdant Catalyst on Grass Block to turn it into Mycelium, or on Mycelium to turn it back into Grass Block. Use it on Dirt with water immediately above to make Clay. Dry Dirt refuses; the water must be over the clicked block.

Flowers, saplings, leaves and ordinary growing crop blocks instead become a random magical plant from the Verdant Catalyst selection. The Spirit World adds Nether Wart to that selection. Each successful transformation replaces the clicked block and consumes one catalyst. Check the clicked block and water position when a use has no effect.
manual.warlockery.herbology.ingredient_r:
Hold use to drink Redstone Soup, even when your hunger bar is full. Finishing takes a little over a second, consumes one serving and returns a Bowl.

Finish drinking with a full hunger bar to gain Health Boost II for three minutes and heal four hearts. The boost supplies four extra hearts of maximum health while it lasts. If you finish while hungry, the soup only provides its ordinary food value: one hunger icon and a little saturation. Fill your hunger bar before drinking when you want the health reward.
manual.warlockery.conjuration.broken_hex:
Place the Statue of Broken Hexes to establish an active ward against incoming hexes within 64 blocks. The protection covers the surrounding area and requires no offering. Use the statue to check its ward message.

Touching this statue does not sever an existing hex. For a hex already affecting you, use the corresponding cure rite described in Circle Magic. Keep the statue in place to maintain its surrounding ward.
manual.warlockery.conjuration.ingredient: Demonic Contract: Binding and Favor

Craft a Demonic Contract with paper, Odd Raw Porkchop and string; its recipe is here. Call a Flame Imp with the summoning rite in Summoned Allies, then use the contract on that unowned imp while you have at least 25 experience levels. Binding consumes one contract and 25 levels, records you as its owner and clears its attack target. Another player's imp refuses a new owner.

Feed your bound imp an Amethyst Shard, Diamond, Emerald, Gold Ingot, Netherite Scrap or Demon Heart by using the gift on it. Each gift is consumed and raises favor by one, to a maximum of six. The message reports its favor. Spell use requires enough favor but does not spend that favor.

Craft a named spell contract using the recipes in this chapter, then use it on your bound imp. An ordinary Demonic Contract only binds; it is not a spell. A named contract used for the first binding is consumed as the binding payment instead of casting, so bind with the ordinary contract first.

An ordinary newly crafted spell contract targets the last creature you hit, otherwise the last creature that hurt you, otherwise you. To select another creature, strike that living target before offering the spell to your imp. Looking at a creature does not select it. A valid sympathetic binding already carried by a contract takes priority. Keep the target in the imp's dimension; insufficient favor or a target in another dimension refuses the spell without consuming it. Read the individual spell before choosing a target.
Fiery Touch: Imp Contract

Combine a Demonic Contract and Blaze Powder to make one Fiery Touch contract. Use it on your own bound Flame Imp with at least one favor. It ignites the selected target for twenty seconds, then consumes the contract. Fire immunity can prevent the burning.

Read Demonic Contract: Binding and Favor for target selection. With no recorded target the spell aims at you, so select the intended creature first when using this harmful spell. The favor remains available for later contracts.
Evaporation: Imp Contract

Combine a Demonic Contract and a dry Sponge to make one Evaporation contract. Offer it to your own bound Flame Imp with at least two favor. It removes up to 64 water-containing blocks around the selected target, reaching three blocks horizontally and two vertically. Waterlogged blocks themselves are removed too.

The working is centered on the selected creature or you, not on the block you look at. Read Demonic Contract: Binding and Favor for that selection. Casting consumes one contract even if no water is found; the imp's favor is retained.
Fiery Tolerance: Imp Contract

Combine a Demonic Contract and Magma Cream to make one Fiery Tolerance contract. Use it on your own bound Flame Imp with at least two favor to give the selected target thirty minutes of Fire Resistance.

The contract is consumed and the imp keeps its favor. Read Demonic Contract: Binding and Favor before casting: a retained combat target receives the protection before you do. With no recorded target, the spell protects you.
Melting Touch: Imp Contract

Combine a Demonic Contract and a Lava Bucket to make one Melting Touch contract; crafting leaves an empty Bucket. Offer the contract to your own bound Flame Imp with at least three favor. A player receiving the spell gains thirty minutes of smelting touch.

During that time, break ores whose ordinary drops have a furnace-smelting result. Those drops are replaced by their smelted products. The spell follows the target-selection rules on Demonic Contract: Binding and Favor; giving it to a creature that cannot mine provides no mining benefit. Casting consumes the contract but keeps the imp's favor.
Living Flame: Imp Contract

Combine a Demonic Contract and a Blaze Rod to make one Living Flame contract. Use it on your own bound Flame Imp with at least four favor. It summons a Blaze beside the selected target and sets that Blaze to attack the target.

The new Blaze is hostile, not a bound familiar. With no recorded combat target, the spell selects you. Read Demonic Contract: Binding and Favor and choose the intended target before offering this contract. Each cast consumes one contract while retaining favor.
Torment: Imp Contract

Combine a Demonic Contract and a Nether Star to make one Torment contract. Offer it to your own bound Flame Imp with all six favor to summon an Abyssal Regent beside you. This spell's arrival follows the caster, rather than the selected target's position.

The Regent is unbound and dangerous. Leave room and prepare before casting; the spell does not give you ownership or an order over it. Casting consumes one contract but keeps the imp's favor. A player-killed Regent drops a Soul of Torment, whose separate guide explains its use. This spell does not call the urn-dropping Emberhorn Archfiend.
manual.warlockery.infusions.ingredient_b:
At a crafting table, combine four ordinary Arrows with a Bone, Glowstone Dust and Ghast Tear to make four Bone Bolts. Put each arrow into its own crafting square; their arrangement does not matter.

Carry Bone Bolts as ammunition for a bow or crossbow. Put them in your off hand while aiming the weapon to select them ahead of other carried arrows, then fire normally. They use the weapon's ordinary aiming and projectile mechanics; using a held bolt by itself does not fire it.

A Bone Bolt's consecrated hit deals one and a half times the normal incoming damage against Warlockery's undead, demons, spirits and Hex Bats, before other applicable protections. This includes vampire creatures, Corpses and Abyssal Regents. The bonus is tied to those creatures; it does not grant a general damage increase against every target or every player with a supernatural form.

At a crafting table, combine four ordinary Arrows and one wooden plank to make four Wooden Bolts. Place each arrow in its own crafting square; any plank type and any arrangement work.

Load them as ordinary bow or crossbow ammunition. Keeping the bolts in your off hand selects them ahead of other carried arrows while you use the weapon. Aim and fire normally; holding and using a bolt alone does not launch it.

Their wooden point deals double incoming damage to Ents, Bramble Colossi and Thorned Pursuers, before other applicable protections. They are not the handheld Wooden Stake used for a sleeping vampire, and this bolt's wooden bonus does not apply to vampire creatures. Choose Bone Bolts for the documented consecrated attack instead.
